transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-29
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jordan Mills (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Skybound Head of Cloud), Devon Lee (Skybound Platform Eng), Anika Bose (Skybound Security), Samir Patel (Skybound PM)

Auto-generated summary: quick technical onboarding to get Skybound onto Redwood marketplace listing + private deployment integration. Some sections are noisy; names and acronyms may be off.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to run through the integration roadmap for the marketplace listing and the private deployment options. we'll cover network, kms, quant, and a benchmark pilot.
00:18 Marta: thanks, alex. quick context—Skybound Edge is rolling out a managed inference offering for telco partners, need marketplace listing for our customers to subscribe easily. key constraints: data residency in eu-west, and strict HSM KMS policies for keys, plus offline edge nodes that occasionally sync.
00:40 Alex: got it. when you say offline edge nodes, do you mean completely air-gapped or just intermittent connectivity?
:48 Devon: mostly intermittent. some nodes operate on customer premises with limited egress, they can reach our control plane but not external internet, so we need a private package or connector.
01:05 Priya: ok that maps to Redwood Private mode — we have two patterns: a VPC connector plus a minimal on-prem runtime, or a full on-prem package. for marketplace listing we usually publish a package that supports VPC peering or static egress.
01:28 Samir: question, for the marketplace listing do customers get billed through Redwood or through Skybound? we need to clarify the billing flow.
01:35 Alex: great question. we support both models; for marketplace we'd typically surface an integration pattern: either Redwood handles metering and revenue share, or you offer your own subscription and call Redwood APIs in the backend. depends on commercial terms. we'll send the pricing/metering doc.
01:52 Anika: security wise our auditors need to see key management flow — we can't have keys exported to external clouds. is KMS/HSM supported in the private deployment?
02:05 Priya: yes. Private supports customer-managed KMS via dedicated key encryption, we have examples for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure KeyVault, and we also support HSM-backed keys via bring-your-own HSM. we'll share the runbook but need your HSM model and certs to confirm.
02:30 Jordan: small note — sometimes the transcript distorts 'KV cache' into 'K V cash' in our docs, so we'll be explicit in the runbook about KV cache behavior and local disk persistence.
02:45 Devon: good — about performance: we are cost-sensitive for edge inference. what quantization profiles does Redwood recommend for smaller GPUs?
02:54 Priya: for 8GB-class GPUs we suggest int8 quant with the QAT-lite path, or 4-bit when quality allows; we provide precompiled variants: fullfp16, int8, quart—sorry sometimes 4bit—variants that trade latency/cost for quality. we'll recommend model family matches.
03:22 Marta: and how does that affect cache/kv behavior? if we use smaller quantized models, are we still able to use prefix caching?
03:31 Priya: yes, prefix caching and KV cache works across variants as long as the model architecture is compatible. we do have fallback policies: if a variant is incompatible, requests can be routed to a compatible hosted variant—tradeoff is higher egress.
03:50 Devon: routing policies — can we define a rule: prefer local private variant, fallback to dedicated region, then hosted? we need that for our SLA.
03:58 Alex: absolutely that's supported. policy config is per-route in the Console, with percentage-based canaries and automatic fallback thresholds. we'll demo that in the next session.
04:12 Samir: for the marketplace artifact, what files are required? container image, helm chart, and some metadata?
04:18 Priya: yes, typically: Helm chart for the connector, image with runtime, a listing manifest with supported regions, and a compliance bundle. plus a small integration test that validates KMS connectivity and a basic inference query.
04:35 Anika: about audit logs — we need end-to-end logs for model inferences redacted PII. does Redwood provide an audit log export to our SIEM?
04:45 Jordan: yes we integrate with syslog/Splunk/Datadog. logs include request id, model id, time, token counts; for PII redaction we have built-in filters but you'll likely want to add a post-processing step on your side.
05:05 Marta: timeline wise, what is realistic to get a marketplace listing live?
05:12 Alex: with a pilot already prepared, usually 6-8 weeks: 1-2 weeks for packaging + security review, 1 week for marketplace QA, 2-4 weeks for certification and listing. if you want faster we can run a pre-cert sanity check.
05:30 Devon: ok that's fine — we want to aim for end of Q1, so early April.
05:40 Priya: let's talk benchmarks — we recommend a 3-test suite: latency p50/p95 for 1-16 concurrent connections, throughput with 8k token windows, and tokenized cost per thousand tokens. we'll send a standard harness.
05:58 Alex: and we'll include sample prompts that approximate telco workloads (summarization of call logs, policy rerank).
06:10 Anika: security again — is RBAC granular? we need to lock who can change routing policies and who can view raw transcripts.
06:20 Priya: yes RBAC is role-based and audit-trailable. you can scope a role to routes, models, and keys. for sensitive artifacts we recommend an encryption-at-rest + restricted role.
06:37 Marta: about private control plane: do we host the control plane in your managed region or do you hand over a control plane bundle? we have a legal preference for a customer-managed control plane in EU for some clients.
06:48 Alex: we offer both: hosted control plane with VPC peering for easier ops, or you can deploy a private control plane that you manage. the private option has more ops effort but meets residency commitments.
07:05 Devon: technical detail: network egress — are there specific ports or NAT patterns the connector uses? we need to reconcile with our network team.
07:12 Jordan: primary egress is HTTPS outbound to the Redwood serving endpoints over 443; we also support private peering with direct IP ranges. we'll share the IP ranges list and a Terraform snippet for peer setup.
07:30 Samir: any known gotchas during marketplace listing? I remember a partner had an issue with image size and helm chart hooks.
07:38 Priya: yep watch the image layering and startup probes in helm, and ensure health endpoints respond quickly. marketplace QA will run a smoke test that includes KMS handshake and a short inference call. failing those can block listing.
07:55 Marta: ok let's map responsibilities: Redwood provides checklist+runbooks, Skybound provides topology and certs.
08:02 Alex: noted. we're going to produce an integration playbook that includes: checklist, benchmark harness, KMS runbook, sample Terraform, and a pre-cert QA script.
08:17 Devon: regarding quantization, could priya share expected accuracy deltas for our model family? we'll need to validate before switching to 4-bit.
08:25 Priya: yes we'll run a small eval on representative prompts. generally int8 is safe for classification/ranking and 4-bit is good for many generative tasks with small quality hit. we'll provide delta estimates once we see your test prompts.
08:43 Anika: auditors will want to see key rotation policies — do you support automatic rotation with customer-managed policies?
08:50 Alex: yes rotation is supported, we log rotations and can provide rotation history in the audit bundle. if you use BYO-HSM there's an extra step to confirm rotation flow.
09:02 Marta: what about fallback metrics? if a local node goes offline and falls back to hosted, how do we track cost impact?
09:12 Alex: Console gives token-level cost and route-level attribution. you can tag requests by customer and get a delta view during fallback events. we'll show sample dashboards.
09:25 Devon: ok, pilot details — what sample workload size should we run?
09:30 Priya: for an edge pilot we recommend 3 nodes with mixed concurrency: 5, 20, and 50 concurrent threads for 24 hours each, with a mix of short chat-style and longer summarization prompts. that'll exercise latency and throughput.
09:50 Samir: for the pilot do we need to sign any extra NDA? we already have an MSA but not sure about data handling specifics.
10:00 Alex: if you're sending production-like data we can add a data processing appendix to the MSA; we'll coordinate with legal.
10:08 Anika: please cc legal on the runbook.
10:11 Alex: will do.
10:16 Jordan: quick demo follow-up — we can record a short screencast showing the canary rollout and route policy in console, want that included?
10:22 Marta: yes please, that'd be helpful for our ops team.
10:27 Devon: one more tiny detail — do you support model packaging with quantized weights baked into the image? we prefer pre-quantized images to save on setup time.
10:36 Priya: yes pre-quantized images are supported, just annotate the manifest with quant metadata and we add it to the catalog. be sure to include reproducible build notes.
10:50 Samir: are there any partner incentives for early listing? discounts or co-marketing support?
10:56 Alex: growth will share co-marketing options; discounts are negotiable on committed Dedicated capacity. I'll loop in partnerships.
11:05 Marta: ok, that's a lot, let's recap next steps.
11:10 Alex: recap - Redwood to share checklist + KMS runbook + terraform snippet + benchmark harness by next Tuesday (2026-02-02). Skybound to share topology and compliance list by Friday (2026-02-03). Schedule pilot week tentatively 2026-02-16 to 02-20. follow-up meeting 2026-02-09 14:00 UTC.
11:32 Devon: sounds good. thanks everyone.
11:36 Alex: thanks all, we'll send notes and action items.

End of transcript. Some names and acronyms may be slightly garbled by automatic transcription (e.g., K V cache, QAT-lite pronounced as 'cat light').
